questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The subjects. I wanted to take courses in Criminology and International law, and KU Leuven by far had the best and most interesting courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: KU Leuven is a wonderful university with amazing professors, but KU Leuven is spot much more than that. Leuven is a vibrant small city with many social opportunities. My exchange exceeded all my expectations and I am so happy that I chose to study at KU Leuven.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy and accessible.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Informative e-mails from the Faculty

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it through Facebook

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is further away, but I was lucky enough that I got to live in a beautiful house - much bigger than students accommodations and even cheaper.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was easy and very accessible. Had to fill out a form online and the I received an answer

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had questions about the process which were promptly answered.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful - I got all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask for help and follow the instructions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very pleased with the selection.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Though almost all of my classes were at KA level, I found the classes weren't too difficult to follow, because I already had had similar courses at my home university. The classes at KU Leuven acted as an interesting opportunity to explore new topics and to look at more specific topics in depth.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different - KU Leuven only had lectures whereas my home university has both lectures and in-depth seminars with a lot more home work and presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Victimology and the Criminal Justice System
- Psychology and the Criminal Justice System 
- Terrorism, Organized Crime and Corporate Crime
- Law of International Organizations
- Humanitarian and Security Law form a Humanitarian Perspective
- Discrimination Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of my courses were very interesting but I would especially recommend Terrorism, Organized Crime and Corporate Crime. It was very insightful and completely flipped my view of law.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Costs to ESN events and having to pay for a gym membership through the Sports Card, even though I already had a sportscard (additional cost).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Books were less expensive than expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I can highly recommend getting a culture card and going to events at STUK

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Events through STUK, Musemnight, thorough orientation days programmed with Belgian Cultural nights, Pub Crawl, Karaoke night and other events throughout the year. I felt very lucky that we had so many opportunities available too us and that social well-being was a large interest.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: As emanation, definitely get the culture card and go to events at STUK

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Coffee at Madmum, walk around Arenberg castle and Abdij Van Park, see Saint-Pierters Church, go to a concert at STUK, have a cheap sandwich at Pain Louvain, eat pizza at Giuditta, take the train to Brussels, Bruges, Antwerp or Gent.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy as it is similar to the Danish culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Keep an open mind

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not all, but a majority of Belgian Flemish students were racist, disrespectful, rude and sexually inappropriate. It is not all of them, but some have a sense of elf entitlement and will say "speak Flemish, you're in Belgium"

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Beer culture, fries and the mix of French and Dutch cuisine

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go to as many orientation events as you can, read throughout the semester so that it doesn't pile up and have fun!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No :)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all over the world, gathering at ESN events and taking weekend trips to see Belgium and to London, Paris and Amsterdam

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To keep up with the reading load and the exam format, which was very different from our exams at UCPH

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
